app.title: DF-XRM visualization: plan the geometry of a dark-field X-ray microscopy experiment
app.summary: The person picks a crystal structure, either by uploading a .cif file or by choosing one from a list, and sets the beam energy and the sample's size in a sidebar. The interface plots the attenuation length and the transmission through the sample, and lists the reflections the crystal allows with their scattering angle, intensity and d-spacing. The person picks a reflection and the sample's up and exit faces. The interface then draws the sample, crystal lattice, beam, lens and goniometer stage in a 3D scene that can be rotated, and reports the stage angles and 2θ. They can load a lens-box configuration to work out the lens distances and magnification, then save the whole plan as a PDF or as a 3D model for Blender.

task.text: Work out, before a beamtime, whether a crystal sample suits dark-field X-ray microscopy and how the sample, stage and lenses must be aligned to image a chosen reflection.

data.text: A crystal structure file and a handful of experiment settings: beam energy, sample dimensions, a chosen reflection, the crystal directions of the sample's faces, and an optional lens-box configuration file. From these the interface computes derived quantities and a 3D scene.
data.item: one planned experiment: a crystal sample in a beam, aligned on one reflection

stage.text: planning the geometry of a diffraction imaging experiment, before beamtime

mechanism.text: Sidebar inputs for energy, sample size, reflection and crystal directions feed a top-to-bottom page that recomputes on every change: material properties, attenuation plots, a reflection table, the derived stage angles and a rotatable 3D scene of the experiment. A lens-configuration file adds an annotated optics diagram, and the whole plan can be exported as a PDF or a Blender model.

field.text: planning the alignment of dark-field X-ray microscopy experiments at a synchrotron

workflow.name: set up an experiment's geometry from a few parameters and export the plan

steps.here: Upload a .cif crystal structure or pick one of several known crystals, which are fetched from an open crystallography database; formula, density and cell parameters are shown

steps.step: set the conditions the plan depends on
steps.here: Enter beam energy in keV or wavelength in Å (each updates the other), plus sample thickness, height and width in µm

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Attenuation length against energy and transmission against thickness are plotted, with the chosen energy and thickness marked, to judge whether enough flux gets through

steps.step: choose one option from the computed candidates
steps.here: A table lists every allowed reflection with 2θ, relative intensity and d-spacing; the brightest reflection is the default Q vector, and the person can type another (h,k,l)

steps.step: lay out the setup and check it visually
steps.here: Sample up and exit faces are set as (h,k,l) or [u,v,w]; the interface solves k0 and kh, reports 2θ and the stage angles φ, χ and ω, and draws sample, lattice, beam, lens and goniometer in a rotatable 3D scene

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Load a .lens file or a sample lens box and a sample-detector distance; the optics are solved for d1, d2 and magnification and drawn on an annotated diagram with the lens mount point
Tick 'make pdf' to get a report with the settings, plots, 3D view, reflection table and optics diagram; download a pickled 3D scene with a Blender import script, or a .blend file directly

distinctive: The output is a set of instrument settings, goniometer angles φ, χ and ω and lens distances, to apply during alignment, not a result about the data
Directions can be given as reciprocal-lattice planes (h,k,l) or real-space directions [u,v,w], and only the component orthogonal to Q or to 'up' is kept
The 3D scene uses parallel projection so the crystal axes can be compared directly with the sample axes
Lens-box configurations are TOML files; any parameter the calculation does not use is reported back to the person
Absorption is checked against sample thickness at the chosen energy before any alignment is planned

parts.title: Experiment settings sidebar
parts.summary: Holds every input for the plan: energy or wavelength, sample dimensions, the Q vector, the sample's up and exit directions, the beam exit direction, lens display and visualization options.

parts.title: Crystal structure input and properties
parts.summary: Lets the person upload a .cif file or choose a known crystal, then shows its formula, density and unit-cell parameters.

parts.title: Attenuation and transmission plots
parts.summary: Plots attenuation length against energy and transmission against thickness, with the chosen energy and thickness marked, so the person can judge whether enough flux leaves the sample.

parts.title: Reflection table
parts.summary: Lists every allowed reflection up to a maximum 2θ, with scattering angle, intensity relative to the brightest reflection and d-spacing, so the person can pick the reflection to image.

parts.title: 3D experiment geometry and stage angles
parts.summary: Solves the incoming and scattered beam directions for the chosen reflection and sample orientation, reports 2θ and the goniometer angles, and draws sample, crystal lattice, beam, lens and stage in a rotatable 3D scene.

parts.title: Lens-box optics diagram
parts.summary: Takes an uploaded or sample lens-box configuration and a sample-detector distance, solves the sample-lens and lens-detector distances and the magnification, and annotates them on a diagram with the lens mount point.

parts.title: PDF report and 3D model export
parts.summary: Builds a PDF of the settings, plots, cropped 3D view, reflection table and optics diagram, and offers download links for a pickled 3D scene with a Blender import script or a .blend file.
